business_problem: Hudson Physicians needed to reduce physician documentation backlog and EHR time in a tight labor market so providers could finish notes faster, improve billing timeliness, and spend more time with patients instead of performing administrative work.
solution_summary: Hudson Physicians deployed Oracle Health AI Agents with Oracle Health Foundation EHR to turn physician conversations and screen interactions into draft clinical documentation and next-step actions. The solution captures visit details on mobile devices, generates notes for review and sign-off, proposes labs and procedure orders, and suggests evaluation and management codes for billing, all inside existing EHR workflows. That design removes the need for providers to act as their own scribes or data miners while also helping staff catch up on coding and billing work that had been delayed for weeks. Because the AI agent is tightly tied to the EHR and future prior-authorization capabilities, Hudson can improve today's documentation burden while also building toward more accurate, payer-aware treatment and billing workflows. The result is better patient face time, lower after-hours charting, and more efficient use of scarce support staff.

solution_components.name: Oracle Health AI Agents
solution_components.role: Captures visit details, drafts notes, suggests orders, and supports coding tasks to reduce physician documentation work.

solution_components.name: Oracle Health Foundation EHR
solution_components.role: Hosts the clinical workflow where AI-generated documentation and proposed actions are reviewed and completed.

data_flow: Visit conversations and screen interactions are captured through Oracle Health AI Agents on physician devices, turned into draft notes, orders, and coding suggestions, then routed into Oracle Health Foundation EHR so providers can finish documentation and billing tasks within their normal workflow.
business_outcome: Hudson Physicians cut documentation time and EHR burden, enabled more than 90% of physicians to finish notes before leaving for the day, reassigned support staff from data entry to patient care, and improved both recruitment and work-life balance for clinicians.

Now more than 90% of physicians finish their notes before leaving for the day.
